text:
Anya: thinking about tenant SLA weighting and a pragmatic runtime we can tweak without redeploys. want to float an idea: 'grace credits' that allow short bursts above reserved qps.
Mike: +1 to having a soft buffer. how do you see it interacting with region preferences and cost caps?
Anya: goal is inventory-aware fallback: if a region is saturated, instead of immediately failing to cheaper model, we drain grace credits and gradually route to fallback. helps avoid thundering.
Kevin: concerned about cross-tenant fairness. if tenant A uses all grace, tenant B shouldn't be starved.
Anya: yep — plan is per-tenant bucket + global emergency pool. priority order: reserved -> grace -> global emergency -> fallback model.
Sophia: how to implement counters w/ low overhead? we need something that works in the router and the runtime.
Anya: propose lightweight leaky-bucket in the policy adapter that emits tokens to the match engine. keeps decision local and compatible with sidecar and gateway.
Mike: can we express this in the policy DSL? something like:
```
policy "tenant_sla" {
  reserved: 100
  grace: {
    rate: 50
    burst: 200
  }
  fallback: "model-small"
}
```
Jen: small nit — define semantics for 'grace' preemption. if grace used in region A, do we block same tenant in region B until refill?
Anya: refill should be global per-tenant across regions; otherwise tenants could game by hitting many regions. but we still track per-region instantaneous load for routing.
Kevin: what about cost caps? If grace shifts traffic to more expensive hardware, we need billing signals to respect per-tenant cost budgets.
Sophia: attach a budget check in the router: if projected cost > tenant_budget -> force fallback to cheaper variant regardless of grace.
Mike: how to signal when a fallback is 'acceptable' quality? can we attach an eval delta threshold to policy?
Anya: yes, add optional quality_delta field. e.g., quality_delta: 0.05 means only fallback if eval degradation <= 5%.
Jen: rolling out this will be tricky. propose staged enablement: 1) simulation mode (dry-run scoring), 2) canary on <10 tenants, 3) platform-wide.
Deploy Bot: deploy scheduled to infra-dev at 2026-04-02T22:00Z for the new policy adapter image :rocket:
Mike: simulation harness should produce per-tenant P95 latency and cost deltas. also show how many grace tokens would be consumed in historic traces.
Anya: i'll make a spike to add simulation scoreboard. next steps: spike + DSL extension PR, then runtime leaky-bucket impl. anyone want to pair on the runtime piece?
Kevin: i'll take runtime. can start tomorrow.
Sophia: i'll own the policy DSL tests and the eval gating.
Jen: i'll draft the rollout checklist and tenant communication template. add metric names: routing.grace.tokens_used, routing.grace.refill_rate, routing.fallback.count.
Anya: thanks — pairing plan: Kevin + Anya on runtime, Sophia on DSL, Mike on simulation harness, Jen on rollout. calling this "grace-credit routing" for short. :ok_hand:
Mike: one more thing — consider ephemeral preemption: if global emergency pool drains, we should degrade non-SLAs first. policy should have a per-tenant criticality flag.
Anya: noted. will add 'tier' tag: critical / standard / best_effort and tie-breaker rules for emergency pool.
Kevin: should we expose two knobs for customers: grace_size and refill_rate? API team will want to keep API surface small.
Jen: recommend starting with refill_rate only; we can auto-calc grace_size from refill_rate * burst_window.
Anya: agreed. i'll draft the DSL and an RFC summary for next arch sync.
Sophia: sounds good. moving to follow-up: create tickets for DSL PR, runtime spike, simulation dataset, rollout plan.
thread_text_summary: Runtime plan for per-tenant 'grace credits' to smooth routing under saturation. Discussed DSL, leaky-bucket implementation, cross-region refill, cost caps, quality gating, rollout stages, owners, and metrics.
